subject: ACME Retail — infra & instrumentation action plan / SDK + observability
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Tom Huang <tom.huang@acme-retail.com>, Sara Lopez <sara@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: ACME Retail — infra & instrumentation action plan / SDK + observability

Hi Tom / Sara —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick post-call recap and proposed next steps focused on the integration areas you flagged: SDK bootstrap/auth, routing for regional and fallback variants, structured output/tool-calls, embeddings/reranking, and observability hooks (trace IDs, logging fields, token-level latency breakdowns).

Recap (what we heard):
- Primary use: product search augmentation + dynamic merchandising (embedding-based reranks on top of existing catalog).
- Constraint: 99th percentile latency target 120ms for user queries, SLO for background batch reranks is 2s.
- Security: SOC2 + IP scoping; your security team will run the standard questionnaire.

Action items / proposal (high level):
1) SDK & auth: provide a small reference repo and 3 auth patterns (API key short-lived, platform token via OIDC, and VPC private endpoint). We'll include code snippets for Node + Python that show token refresh and KV cache warm-up. (Attachment: redwood-sdk-auth-snippets.txt)
2) Routing & model variants: recommend an edge routing policy — region by client IP, then model-tier fallback (fast quantized variant -> full model). We'll supply the policy template you can drop into your config.
3) Structured output & tool-calls: for product catalog actions we suggest using structured tool-calling with a deterministic JSON schema to avoid hallucination. We'll include an example for "product_match" + confidence fields and post-processing rules.
4) Embeddings & reranker: propose two-step flow: cheap ANN candidate retrieval -> cross-encoder rerank. We recommend 1536-d embeddings (faiss index) with per-request top-k=50 then rerank top-10.
5) Observability & tracing: provide headers and logging field conventions: X-Trace-Id (UUID v4 propagated), X-RW-Request-Id (short id), and X-RW-Latency-Breakdown (tokenization|inference|postproc in ms). Also provide library helpers that emit token-level timing at debug level to your logs and a dashboard query for 95/99 latency slices.

Next steps:
- Ben -> share snippet pack, instrumentation checklist, and a draft routing policy by EOD today.
- Acme -> confirm which auth pattern you want us to prioritize (api-key / oidc / vpc) and share the security contact.
- Schedule a 30m follow-up next week to walk through the integration repo and log examples.

Proposed follow-up times: Thu 11/19 10:00am PT or Fri 11/20 1:00pm PT — please confirm.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-auth-snippets.txt, integration-observability-checklist.csv

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

--
Redwood Inference — developer-first inference runtime

Ben —

Appreciate the clear plan. Two quick clarifications before we sync:
1) For the X-RW-Latency-Breakdown header: will Redwood emit a single header per response with three numeric ms fields (e.g., tokenization=8;inference=85;postproc=4)? Or is the token-level timing only available via your SDK debug logs? Our perf team needs the header in the response to surface in the CDN logs.
2) For embeddings -> rerank flow, can you confirm the memory footprint estimate for the reranker when holding top-50 candidates per request (we run many concurrent sessions during peak)?

Also looping in security@acmeretail.com (copied) — they will send the questionnaire today.

Tom Huang
Director, Engineering — Search & Merchandising

Subject: Re: ACME Retail — infra & instrumentation action plan / SDK + observability

Tom —

Great questions. Short answers up-front, then a little more detail and the concrete artifacts we'll share.

1) X-RW-Latency-Breakdown header: we will emit a single header on all responses for hosted API customers (and the header is available in Dedicated as an opt-in toggle). Format: tokenization=<ms>;inference=<ms>;postproc=<ms>;total=<ms>. Example: "tokenization=7;inference=93;postproc=4;total=104". We can also include a compact sample of token-level timings in debug logs (per-token timings only at debug to avoid high log volume). We'll add a small middleware snippet that populates the header in Node and Python SDKs.

2) Reranker memory footprint: the cross-encoder reranker (full attention) memory scales roughly with sequence_len * hidden_size * batch. For a top-50 candidate rerank at batch-size=1 and 512 tokens average, estimate ~1.8GB GPU memory for the model we recommended (quantized 8-bit variant will be ~40% smaller). We'll include a table with concrete numbers for candidate sizes 10/20/50 and expected GPU/MEM usage. If you need lower memory, we suggest a two-tier reranker: a light-weight transformer (distilled) for top-50 then a heavy cross-encoder for final top-10.

Artifacts we'll attach (shared now):
- redwood-sdk-auth-snippets.txt — quick start for API-key + OIDC samples.
- integration-observability-checklist.csv — checklist for headers to propagate, sample log fields, and dashboard widget presets.
- security-questionnaire-acme.xlsx (we've received — thanks).

Concrete next steps:
- Ben -> send the routing policy template and a sample middleware that injects X-Trace-Id / X-RW-Request-Id and computes X-RW-Latency-Breakdown (I attached the Node snippet).
- Karthik -> can you produce the memory table for reranker candidate sizes and the quick config for automatic fallback to quantized models? Target: EOD Thu 11/19.
- Marissa -> I'll ask you to lead the SOC2 evidence collection once security@acmeretail.com confirms the exact set; flag me if runbooks are required.

Proposed 30m walkthrough: Thu 11/19 10:00am PT — if that works, I'll send a calendar invite.

Ben

Attachments referenced: redwood-sdk-auth-snippets.txt, integration-observability-checklist.csv

Ben
